D007-D015_h001.question:
It’s been about seven months now that I’ve felt…flat, I guess. At work on the ward, things that used to matter—finishing a shift short-staffed, getting good feedback—barely register. My coworkers comment that I look “worn out.”

Sleep is awful. I wake up around 3 or 4 a.m. every day, completely awake, and just lie there, heavy, dreading the day. That’s usually when the other stuff happens. I’ll see a shadowy figure standing by my bedroom door, or someone sitting on the chair. When I turn on the light, no one’s there. On the bus or at work, I feel like the TV in the break room, the radio songs, even random conversations are aimed at me, hinting that I’ve done something wrong.

When I’m in this low state, my thoughts jump around when I talk, like I lose the thread mid-sentence. But these things only happen when I’m in this depressed phase—there hasn’t been a time I felt okay emotionally while still seeing things or feeling targeted.
